## Introduction

Hierarchical Gamma–Poisson model [@gelman2013bda]: each sample (row) has its own background
rate `br[n] ~ Gamma(a0, b0)` and its counts are Poisson with that rate.
The model `gamma_poisson` is in `src/models.jl` (the miRNA application is in
`05_omics/gse154829_mirna_asthma.qmd`).

## Setup

The analysis runs in Julia [@bezanson2017julia]; `ExposomicsJulia` provides the shared helpers and models, together with DataFrames.jl [@bouchetvalat2023dataframes] and Turing.jl [@ge2018turing].

```{julia}
#| label: setup
using ExposomicsJulia
using Distributions, Statistics, StatsBase, Random, DataFrames
using Turing, Plots
```

## Simulation

Simulated data: 100 samples × 40 counts, background rates from `Gamma(5, 2)`.

```{julia}
#| label: simulation
Random.seed!(1234)
back_distr = rand(Gamma(5.0, 2.0), 100)
X = zeros(100, 40)
for i in 1:100
    X[i, :] = rand(Poisson(back_distr[i]), 40)
end
```

```{julia}
#| label: simulation-2
#| eval: false
m = gamma_poisson(X)
chain_gp = sample(m, NUTS(), MCMCThreads(), 1000, 3)
tmp = chain_summary(chain_gp)
```

Compare the estimated background rates with the simulated ones:

```{julia}
#| label: simulation-3
#| eval: false
scatter(back_distr, posterior_mean(chain_gp, :br);
        xlabel = "true rate", ylabel = "posterior mean", label = "")
```
